defense_analyst.prose: CIN's defense is middling overall. It allows a successful play on 43.7% of snaps [dc1] over 545 plays [dc2], ranking 16th in success rate allowed [dc3] and 14th in EPA per play allowed [dc4]. The run defense is the softer side: -0.03 EPA per run play allowed [dc5] over 196 runs [dc6], against 0.02 EPA per pass play allowed [dc7] over 349 dropbacks [dc8]. For WAS, that favors committing to the run game to set up manageable third downs. The pressure proxy (sacks plus QB hits) is 14.9% of dropbacks [dc9], 21st in the league [dc10]. CIN faced 5+ rushers on 16.9% of dropbacks [dc11] and sacks on 7.5% [dc12]. That is a real but not extreme test for WAS's line, so the protection plan should account for blitz looks without abandoning max protection on obvious passing downs. CIN allows explosive pass plays on 8.9% of attempts [dc13]. Third down is a clear weakness: CIN allows conversions on 46.5% of attempts [dc14], 27th of 32 [dc15]. WAS converts 33.3% on offense [dc16], 30th [dc17], so both sides are poor on third down and the game may turn on who stays on schedule. In the red zone, CIN allows touchdowns on 40.0% of drives [dc18] over only 30 drives [dc19], while WAS scores on 59.1% [dc20] over 22 drives [dc21]. Both red-zone samples are small and should be weighted accordingly.

sections.heading: Opponent defense
sections.body: Cincinnati's defense is middling overall, allowing a successful play on 43.7% of snaps [dc1] over 545 plays [dc2], 16th in the league [dc3]. The run defense is the softer side at -0.03 EPA per run play allowed [dc4] over 196 runs [dc5], so Washington should be willing to commit to the ground game to create manageable third downs. Cincinnati's pressure proxy (sacks plus QB hits) is 14.9% of dropbacks [dc6] over 349 dropbacks [dc7], 21st in the league [dc8], and it brings 5+ rushers on 16.9% of dropbacks [dc9]. Account for blitz looks without abandoning max protection on obvious passing downs. Third down is its clear weakness, as it allows conversions on 46.5% of attempts [dc11] over 114 plays [dc12], 27th in the league [dc13]. Washington converts 33.3% on offense [dc14] over 120 plays [dc15], 30th in the league [dc16], so the game may turn on who stays on schedule. In the red zone, Cincinnati allows touchdowns on 40.0% of drives [dc17] over only 30 drives [dc18], while Washington scores on 59.1% [dc19] over 22 drives [dc20]. Both red-zone samples are small.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: Cincinnati's kicking is steady. E.McPherson has made 92.9% [kc1] of 14 [kc2] field goal tries and 100.0% [kc3] of 6 [kc4] from 50-plus, and he has handled every attempt all season. Washington has made 85.0% [kc5] of 20 [kc6]. Treat Cincinnati's long attempts as live, so a drive that stalls near midfield still gives them a makeable kick. Their punter nets 40.96 yards [kc7] on 26 punts [kc8] and pins 57.7% [kc9] of punts inside the 20, so expect short fields. Kickoffs are touchbacks only 14.3% [kc10] of the time on 56 kickoffs [kc11]. Punt returns average just 4.7 yards [kc14] on 22 returns [kc15], so Washington can punt without much fear of the return.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Cincinnati's latest injury report lists S Kyle Dugger as Out. He has averaged 16.5% of snaps [ic2] over only 4 games [ic3], so expect the other safeties to absorb his role, and his exit thins Cincinnati's safety depth. WR Andrei Iosivas is Doubtful but takes just 1.2% of targets [ic5] on 331 team targets [ic6], so his absence should barely move Cincinnati's pass distribution. CB Jalen Davis is Doubtful; his 61.3% snap average [ic8] comes from only 3 games [ic9], so treat him as a depth question. On Washington's report, TE Colson Yankoff is Out after averaging 14.0% of snaps [ic12] over 8 games [ic13]. C Lucas Patrick is Out after playing 76.9% of snaps [ic17] over 7 games [ic18]. Neither Washington absence is a major change for Cincinnati's game plan.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Third down is the central matchup. Cincinnati converts 51.9% of third downs [mc1] over 104 plays [mc2], and Washington's offense converts only 33.3% [mc5], while Cincinnati's defense allows 46.5% [mc6]. Cincinnati drops back on 79.8% of third downs [mc7], so expect pass-heavy thirds, and Washington's front and coverage must win the long-yardage downs. The run game is the early-down lever. Cincinnati allows -0.03 EPA per run play [mc8] over 196 runs [mc9], against 0.02 EPA per pass play [mc10] over 349 dropbacks [mc11], so Washington should commit to the run early. Red zone is the third matchup. Washington scores on 59.1% of red-zone drives [mc16] over 22 drives [mc17], and Cincinnati scores on 73.0% [mc20] over 37 drives [mc21]. Cincinnati's kicker is 100.0% from 50-plus [mc24] on 6 attempts [mc25], so treat long field goals as live.
